title: Playing the White House: Ellington's birthday, Carter and Reagan
summary: Recollections of Ellington's White House party, Carter's garden party and Reagan's caviar event.

blocks.x: I see a bunch of pictures of you at Ellington’s birthday party at . . .
Which one? At the White House?
At the White House.
Oh yeah.
Give me your recollection of that evening.
That was fun. That was – Willis Conover put that together, and he got almost everybody. I saw – I remember Billy Eckstine and Joe Williams. They were there. Was Pearl Bailey there?
I’m not sure.
I don’t know if Pearl was there or not. But I remember Milt Hinton and Mona. It was a beautiful occasion.
How do you – I think it was 19 – I want to say – 78 when Jimmy Carter did his – did a big party at the White House, I guess it was.
Yeah, and Dizzy had him up singing Salt Peanuts?
Right.

Yeah, that was fun. He was sitting out on the lawn. He had brought up a lot of these New Orleans cooks. They had tables all over the lawn of the White House. Man, we were eating up a storm. Good jambalaya, gumbo, spare ribs, red beans and rice. All the goodies, all the New Orleans goodies. It was just beautiful. Jimmy was sitting there in his shirt-sleeves and was listening to the music, and Dizzy had him come up and sing
[Terry sings Salt Peanuts].
How many times – if you can recollect – have you performed at the White House?

I’ve been there so many times I can’t even – I’d say roughly a dozen times. I was there with Nixon a couple times, with Johnson a couple times, with Lady Bird [Johnson], her Christmas party, with Carter a couple times, and with – what’s the one that succeeded Carter? The Republican?
Reagan.
Yeah. He had a real snobbish party. He had guards that escorted everybody to their seats.
Was this the Lionel Hampton thing?
No, that’s another one. I was there for that one too. Yeah, when – who was it? Illinois Jacquet – somebody was conducting Art Blakey’s drum solo. That was funny.
That was strange, because I think Lionel came out and played something about When It’s Sleepy Time Down South or some song that . . .
. . . Wasn’t too cool. No.
That wasn’t really . . .

Yeah, I’ll never forgot that. Anyhow, what the President said this time, “This time last year you had a party and you stunk up the neighborhood with spare ribs and stuff. This time we’re going to have our party inside, and we’re going to serve caviar,” and he escorted everybody in with the guns and went inside the White House, and there was about enough caviar for you and me to have a mouthful.
